concepts.def: Single unique items made to order: bespoke wedding cakes, custom-built homes; high cost, low volume.
Groups of identical items produced together; e.g. a bakery making 100 loaves before switching to cakes.
Continuous mass production on assembly line; high volume, low unit cost; pioneered by Ford Model T (1908).
Workers grouped into self-managing teams completing a whole product or section; balances flexibility and efficiency.
Machines and software performing tasks previously done by humans; raises productivity but reduces unskilled jobs.
Term coined in Germany 2011: smart factories using IoT, AI, robotics and data analytics to digitise production.
